From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From inversa (“inverse”, adjective) +‎ -o (nominal suffix).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /inˈverso/
  • Rhymes: -erso
  • Syllabification: in‧ver‧so

Noun

[edit]

inverso (accusative singular inverson, plural inversoj, accusative plural inversojn)

  1. inverse

References

[edit]
  • “inverso”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin inversus.

Adjective

[edit]

inverso (feminine inversa, masculine plural inversos, feminine plural inversas)

  1. inverse, opposite, reciprocal

Related terms

[edit]
  • inverter

Further reading

[edit]
  • “inverso”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Esperanto inverso, English inverse, French inverse, German invers, Italian inverso, Spanish inverso. By surface analysis, inversa +‎ -o.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /inˈverso/
  • Hyphenation: in‧ver‧so

Noun

[edit]

inverso (plural inversi)

  1. inverse

References

[edit]
  • inverso in Ido-English Dictionary by L.H. Dyer, 1924

Istriot

[edit]

Preposition

[edit]

inverso

  1. towards (to a direction or place)
    • 1877, Antonio Ive, Canti popolari istriani: raccolti a Rovigno, volume 5, Ermanno Loescher, page 40:
      Vuoltite biunduleîna inverso lai,
      Turn around towards this place, little blonde,

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /inˈvɛr.so/
  • Rhymes: -ɛrso
  • Hyphenation: in‧vèr‧so

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin inversus.

Adjective

[edit]

inverso (feminine inversa, masculine plural inversi, feminine plural inverse)

  1. reverse, inverted, opposite, contrary, inverse, upside down
    Synonyms: invertito, opposto, contrario

Noun

[edit]

inverso m (plural inversi)

  1. the opposite, the contrary
    Synonyms: opposto, contrario
  2. (arithmetic) reciprocal

Etymology 2

[edit]

    By surface analysis, univerbation of in +‎ verso; cognate with French envers.

    Preposition

    [edit]

    inverso (obsolete, poetic)

    1. toward
      Synonyms: verso, incontro a
    Alternative forms
    [edit]
    • inver

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • inversamente
    • inversione
    • inversivo
    • invertire

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • inverso¹ in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana
    • inverso² in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana
    • inverso² in Treccani.it – Enciclopedia Dantesca (1970), Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

    Anagrams

    [edit]
    • nervosi, nevrosi, svinerò, versino, vinsero

    Latin

    [edit]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    Participle

    [edit]

    inversō

    1. dative/ablative masculine/neuter singular of inversus

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    From in- (“against / (intensifier)”) +‎ versō, or alternatively, from invertō (“invert, turn upside down, upset”) +‎ -tō (frequentative suffix).

    Verb

    [edit]

    inversō (present infinitive inversāre, perfect active inversāvī, supine inversātum); first conjugation

    1. to invert

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Latin inversus.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛʁ.su/ [ĩˈvɛh.su]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛʁ.su/ [ĩˈvɛh.su]
      • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛɾ.su/
      • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛʁ.su/ [ĩˈvɛχ.su]
      • (Caipira) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛɻ.su/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛʁ.so/ [ĩˈvɛh.so]
     
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛɾ.su/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩˈvɛɾ.su/
      • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩˈbɛɾ.su/

    • Hyphenation: in‧ver‧so

    Adjective

    [edit]

    inverso (feminine inversa, masculine plural inversos, feminine plural inversas)

    1. inverse; opposite

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • inverter

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “inverso”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

    Spanish

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Latin inversus, perfect passive participle of invertō (“turn upside down”). Doublet of anverso and envés.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /imˈbeɾso/ [ĩmˈbeɾ.so]
    • Rhymes: -eɾso
    • Syllabification: in‧ver‧so

    Adjective

    [edit]

    inverso (feminine inversa, masculine plural inversos, feminine plural inversas)

    1. inverted, reverse
    2. opposite
      Synonym: opuesto

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • a la inversa
    • matriz inversa
    • por la inversa
    • psicología inversa

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • invertir

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “inverso”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
